The omitted proof `⋯` cannot by itself resolve this because the restriction would have to be encoded in the type of `c`. The package needs the fully explicit elaborated body of `contentColGeq`, especially the binder type for `c`. If that type is `{c // c ∈ skewYoungDiagram lam mu ∧ c.2 ≥ j}`, the target is faithful; quantifying `j : ℕ` rather than only positive integers is a harmless strengthening. If no `c.2 ≥ j` restriction is present, the dependency must be changed to count exactly that restricted subtype.

The target states exactly `contentColGeq T 1 = contentTableau T`, matching “cont(col_{≥ 1} T) = cont(T).” By `skewYoungDiagram lam mu = {c | mu c.1 < c.2 ∧ c.2 ≤ lam c.1}`, every cell has a natural-number column `c.2` strictly greater than `mu c.1`, hence at least 1, so the restriction counted by `contentColGeq T 1` contains every cell counted by `contentTableau T`. The elaborated binders `∀ {N : ℕ} {lam mu : Fin N → ℕ} (T : Tableau lam mu)` do not require `lam` and `mu` to be decreasing N-partitions or require `mu ⊆ lam`, unlike the blueprint. This makes the formal theorem strictly more general rather than weaker: it still covers every tableau in the blueprint’s setting. The use of `Fin N` to encode the N entries/labels is an indexing representation, not a mathematically contentful restriction.

The formal hypothesis `∀ (i : Fin N), lam i < j` is exactly the blueprint condition “`j > λ_i` for every row index `i`.” By `skewYoungDiagram`, every cell `c` satisfies `c.2 ≤ lam c.1`; hence under this hypothesis no cell can lie in a column `c.2 ≥ j`. Therefore `contentColGeq T j`, which counts each value in columns `j` and beyond, is the zero function, matching `cont(col_{≥ j} T) = 0`. The formal declaration allows arbitrary functions `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ` rather than only partitions and allows every `j : ℕ` rather than only positive integers; these are wider quantifiers/weaker restrictions, so the theorem is strictly more general rather than weaker.

The formal hypothesis exactly matches the blueprint: `∀ (c : { c // c ∈ skewYoungDiagram lam mu }), T' c = i ↔ T c = i` quantifies over every cell of the common shape and asserts the same pointwise characterization of the cells containing `i`. By definition, `contentTableau T i = Nat.card { c // T c = i }`, so the hypothesis identifies precisely the two fiber types whose cardinalities form the stated content entries, yielding `contentTableau T' i = contentTableau T i`. The formal binders `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ` do not require them to be N-partitions or require `μ ⊆ λ`; this makes the theorem more general than the blueprint rather than weaker, since it still includes the blueprint’s partition-shaped cases. Likewise, representing `[N]` by `Fin N` is an index encoding, not a mathematically contentful restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.det-.justification: The target quantifies over exactly the relevant setting: `∀ {N : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) (MvPolynomial (Fin N) R))`, matching a square matrix over the polynomial ring `R[x₁, …, x_N]` with a commutative coefficient ring. Its hypothesis `(∀ (i j : Fin N), (M i j).IsSymmetric)` is precisely “all entries ... are symmetric polynomials,” since `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric` means invariance under permutations of variables. Its conclusion `M.det.IsSymmetric` is exactly “then det(M) is a symmetric polynomial.” The use of `Fin N` is the standard finite indexing encoding of the blueprint’s `[N]`, and the determinant’s `DecidableEq` and `Fintype` requirements are automatically supplied for `Fin N`, adding no mathematical hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.e-is.justification: All three targets restrict the index to `(n : ℕ)`, while the blueprint definitions declare `e_n`, `h_n`, and `p_n` “for each `n ∈ ℤ`,” and the statement says they are symmetric “for every `n`.” Thus the formal declarations omit all negative indices, a narrowed quantifier. Moreover, the dependency `p` is defined by `MvPolynomial.psum (Fin N) K n`, whose docstring says it is “the sum over all the `n`-th powers of the variables”; at `n = 0` this is a sum of one term per variable, whereas the blueprint explicitly defines `p_0 = 1`. To be faithful, the dependencies `e`, `h`, and `p` should accept `n : ℤ` and implement the blueprint’s negative-index conventions, and `p` must special-case zero as `1` (and negative indices as `0`); the theorem binders should then quantify over `n : ℤ`. The extra `[DecidableEq (Fin N)]` on `h_isSymm` is only computational encoding for `hsymm`, not the decisive mathematical drift.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.ehp-.justification: The elementary-symmetric formula is faithful for natural n: the target sums over `s ∈ Finset.powersetCard n Finset.univ`, exactly the subsets `S ⊆ [N]` with `|S| = n`, and then takes `∏ i ∈ s, MvPolynomial.X i`. The power-sum target, however, quantifies over every natural number via `∀ ... (n : ℕ), ... p n = ∑ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ n`. The informal definition fixes `p_0 = 1`, while the displayed sum at `n = 0` is the sum of one copy of `1` for every variable and is not generally `1`. This mismatch enters through `AlgebraicCombinatorics.SymmetricPolynomials.p`, whose body is `MvPolynomial.psum ... n`, together with the unrestricted binder `(n : ℕ)` in `p_eq_sum_pow`. To be faithful to the blueprint definition, `p_eq_sum_pow` should assume `0 < n`, and `p` should separately represent the stipulated value `p_0 = 1` (and, if the full integer-indexed definition is intended, also the negative case `p_n = 0`).

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.esym.justification: The first target directly matches the blueprint: its binders `∀ {K : Type u_1} [CommRing K] {N : ℕ} (n : ℕ)` cover every natural `n` (hence “for each n ≥ 0”), and its equality is exactly `e_{n+1}(x₁,…,x_N,y) = e_{n+1}(x₁,…,x_N) + y * e_n(x₁,…,x_N)`. Here `MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc` includes the first `N` variables into `Fin (N+1)`, while `MvPolynomial.X (Fin.last N)` is the added last variable `y`. The second target is a stronger, shifted formulation: for every `n` it states the recurrence for `e_n`, with the necessary zero-degree conditional. Instantiating it at `n + 1` makes the condition false and gives `(n + 1) - 1 = n`, recovering the blueprint recurrence. The universally quantified coefficient commutative ring does not weaken the stated polynomial identity.

The formal conclusion exactly matches the recurrence: `MvPolynomial.esymm σ R n = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1), (-1) ^ (j + 1) * MvPolynomial.hsymm σ R j * MvPolynomial.esymm σ R (n - j)`. Since `Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1)` consists precisely of natural numbers `j` with `1 ≤ j ≤ n`, this is the blueprint’s `e_n = ∑_{j=1}^{n} (-1)^{j+1} h_j e_{n-j}`. The hypothesis `0 < n` is exactly “for `n > 0`.” The base-library meanings of `esymm` and `hsymm` agree with the informal definitions as sums of squarefree monomials and all monomials of degree `n`, respectively. Quantification over arbitrary finite `σ` and arbitrary commutative coefficient ring `R` is more general than the stated variables `x₁,…,x_N`, rather than a weakening. `[DecidableEq σ]` is an implementation-level requirement for `hsymm`; on a finite variable set it does not impose a mathematically substantive restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.fill.justification: The blueprint says “For any filling f of Y(λ/μ)” and does not require N ≠ 0, whereas the elaborated signature quantifies only `∀ {N : ℕ} [inst : NeZero N] ...`. This excludes `N = 0`, for which the statement remains meaningful: the unique 0-partitions have an empty diagram, the empty filling exists, and both sides are empty products. The restriction enters through the `[NeZero N]` binder of `SkewFilling`, and consequently also through `fillingMonomial`, `fillingContent`, and `skewYoungDiagram`; it is mathematically contentful rather than merely needed to encode the products. To make the theorem faithful, remove these `NeZero N` binders, using the all-`N` Young-diagram/set-difference construction. Apart from this restriction, `fillingMonomial f = ∏ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ fillingContent f i` exactly matches the stated product over `i = 0, …, N-1`; allowing fillings when `μ ⊈ λ` is only a generalization of the informal statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.geom.justification: The first declaration quantifies over every variable, `∀ {N : ℕ} (i : Fin N)`, matching “For each i,” and states `((1 - PowerSeries.X * PowerSeries.C (MvPolynomial.X i)) * PowerSeries.mk fun k => MvPolynomial.X i ^ k) = 1`. Here `PowerSeries.X` is the power-series variable t, `PowerSeries.C (MvPolynomial.X i)` is the constant series x_i, and `PowerSeries.mk fun k => ... ^ k` has k-th coefficient x_i^k, hence represents `∑_{k≥0} (t x_i)^k`. The second declaration takes products over all `i : Fin N` and states exactly that the product of the `(1 - t x_i)` factors times the product of their geometric series is `1`, matching `E(t) · H(t) = 1`. Its coefficient ring is `MvPolynomial (Fin N) K`, which is the defined polynomial ring `P K N`. Both signatures assume `[CommRing K]`, whereas the supplied informal geometric-series definition mentions a field; this is a strictly more general result with weaker algebraic hypotheses, not drift.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.hori.justification: The blueprint asks for an equivalence between the geometric definition—“μ ⊆ λ and the Young diagram Y(λ/μ) has no two boxes lying in the same column”—and an entry-wise characterization. But `SkewPartition.isHorizontalStrip` is already defined by the entry-wise condition `∀ (i : Fin N) (hi : ↑i + 1 < N), s.inner.parts i ≥ s.outer.parts ⟨↑i + 1, hi⟩`, exactly the body of `isHorizontalStripFun s.outer.parts s.inner.parts`. Thus the target unfolds to the entry-wise condition iff itself, and never states the geometric side of the intended equivalence. The difference enters through the body of `SymmetricFunctions.SkewPartition.isHorizontalStrip`; it should instead encode the no-two-boxes-in-a-column condition (with containment supplied by the bundle), while `isHorizontalStripFun` remains the entry-wise condition. Additionally, the binder `s : SkewPartition N` restricts to pairs carrying `inner ≤ outer`, whereas Definition def.sf.strips initially permits arbitrary pairs and includes containment in horizontal-striphood. For a theorem over arbitrary pairs, the entry-wise side would need to include `μ ≤ λ`; alternatively the blueprint statement would need to explicitly restrict to contained pairs.

The blueprint says membership holds iff “μ ⊆ λ, λ/μ is a horizontal strip, and |λ| - |μ| = n.” These are represented respectively by `∀ (i : Fin N), mu.parts i ≤ lam.parts i`, `isHorizontalStripFun lam.parts mu.parts`, and `hasSizeDiff mu.parts lam.parts n`, whose body is `∑ i, lam i = ∑ i, mu i + n`. The formal RHS additionally requires `∀ i, lam.parts i ≤ horizontalStripUpperBound mu n i`, but this is redundant: for `i > 0` it is exactly implied by the horizontal-strip inequality `lam_i ≤ mu_{i-1}`, while for `i = 0` it follows from containment of every part together with the total size increase `n`; for `N = 0` it is vacuous. Thus the added conjunct does not narrow the characterized partitions, and the formal and informal statements have the same mathematical content.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.hsym.justification: The blueprint says that “for any n ∈ ℤ” the extended complete homogeneous polynomial is symmetric, meaning “for any permutation σ of Fin N, we have σ(h_n) = h_n.” The elaborated target universally quantifies exactly the relevant data, `∀ {N : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (n : ℤ)`, and concludes `(SymmetricFunctions.hsymmExt n).IsSymmetric`. By the base-library definition, `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric` means invariance under permutations of variables via `rename`, matching the blueprint’s notion of symmetry. Moreover, `hsymmExt` is defined as `if 0 ≤ n then MvPolynomial.hsymm (Fin N) R n.toNat else 0`, matching the informal extension: the usual complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial for nonnegative indices and zero for negative indices (with `h_0 = 1` supplied by `hsymm`). The `CommRing R` assumption and `N : ℕ` are precisely the fixed coefficient-ring and finite-variable setting specified by the informal definitions, not added restrictions.

The conclusion exactly matches the blueprint recurrence: Lean states `MvPolynomial.hsymm σ R n = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1), (-1) ^ (j + 1) * MvPolynomial.esymm σ R j * MvPolynomial.hsymm σ R (n - j)`, while `Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1)` is precisely the natural-number range `j = 1, …, n`. The library meanings of `hsymm` (“sum over all the degree n monomials”) and `esymm` (“sum over all the degree n squarefree monomials”) agree with the informal definitions of `h_n` and `e_n`. The hypothesis `0 < n` is exactly “for n > 0.” Although the informal definitions index by integers, positive integer indices are exactly represented by positive naturals, so `(n : ℕ)` does not omit any case covered by this recurrence. The binders `[Fintype σ]` and `[DecidableEq σ]` encode the finite variable set `[N]` and the decidability needed by the polynomial implementation. Allowing any finite variable type `σ` and any coefficient commutative ring `[CommRing R]` is a harmless generalization of the fixed finite-variable symmetric-polynomial setting, not a weakening by added mathematical hypotheses.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.inte.justification: The piecewise value clauses are represented correctly: `pZ` has `if n > 0 then ... p n.toNat else if n = 0 then 1 else 0`, while `hZ` and `eZ` use the corresponding natural-indexed polynomial when `0 ≤ n` and `0` otherwise. The `[DecidableEq (Fin N)]` binder of `hZ` is only computational support required by `MvPolynomial.hsymm`, not a mathematically substantive restriction. However, the blueprint also explicitly asserts: “All are symmetric for every $n \in \mathbb Z$.” Every target merely returns `AlgebraicCombinatorics.SymmetricPolynomials.P K N`, whose body is `MvPolynomial (Fin N) K`, the full polynomial ring. The package supplies neither a subtype corresponding to the blueprint’s `\mathcal S` nor a formal predicate expressing invariance under permutations, so this final assertion cannot be stated with the available project definitions. To make the package faithful, add a definition of symmetric polynomials (as a predicate or subtype) and either make `eZ`, `hZ`, and `pZ` land in that subtype or add declarations proving that each is symmetric for every integer index.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.jt-d.justification: The target states exactly the determinant equality from the blueprint: “The determinant of the Jacobi–Trudi matrix equals the determinant of the LGV path weight matrix: det(H) = det(M).” Its signature equates `(SymmetricFunctions.jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam mu).det` with the determinant of `LGV.pathWeightMatrix ... jacobiTrudiArcWeight (jacobiTrudiSourceVertex mu) (jacobiTrudiTargetVertex lam)`. The dependency bodies give the intended entries, path-weight sums, integer lattice, arc weights, and source/target vertices. The binders `∀ {N : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (lam mu : Fin N → ℕ)` impose no extra mathematical hypothesis; allowing arbitrary tuples rather than only partitions is strictly more general. The use of `Fin N` introduces zero-based indexing, but the resulting common horizontal translation of all stated source and target vertices preserves the path-weight matrix because the lattice and weights are horizontally translation-invariant.

The formal theorem is restricted by the binders `hlam : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i`, `hmu : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → mu j ≤ mu i`, and `hcontained : ∀ i, mu i ≤ lam i`. The informal theorem only states “The determinant of the Jacobi–Trudi matrix equals the sum of nipat weights” and its informal nipat definition describes paths and the column-strictness condition without assuming that `lam` and `mu` are weakly decreasing or that `mu ≤ lam`. The supplied definition of an `N`-partition explains that concept but does not assert that the theorem’s `λ` and `μ` are such partitions. Thus these are mathematically contentful added hypotheses, making the Lean theorem weaker. The restriction enters both the target and, more fundamentally, `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat`, whose parameters require `hlam`, `hmu`, and `hcontained`. To match the stated blueprint, `Nipat` and the theorem should be generalized to arbitrary `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ` (allowing an empty path type when endpoints make paths impossible), or the blueprint statement must explicitly restrict `λ, μ` to `N`-partitions with `μ ⊆ λ`. The arbitrary `[CommRing R]` is not a problem: it makes the coefficient setting more general.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.jt-l.justification: The elaborated theorem is restricted by the mathematically substantive binders `hlam : ∀ ... lam j ≤ lam i`, `hmu : ∀ ... mu j ≤ mu i`, and `hcontained : ∀ i, mu i ≤ lam i`. The informal statement merely asserts `∑_{p LGV-nipat} w(p) = ∑_{p nipat} w(p)`, and its definition of `nipat` specifies endpoints and column-strictness but does not require that `lam` and `mu` be weakly decreasing or that `mu_i ≤ lam_i`. The supplied definition of an `N`-partition explains that term, but the statement never declares `lam` and `mu` to be N-partitions; likewise, no informal definition imposes containment. The restriction enters both the target binders and the dependency `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat`, whose type itself requires `hlam`, `hmu`, and `hcontained`. To be faithful, either the blueprint must explicitly assume that `lam` and `mu` are N-partitions with `mu ⊆ lam`, or `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat` and the theorem must be generalized to arbitrary `lam mu`, representing genuine lattice paths (and hence correctly handling impossible endpoints). The arbitrary `[CommRing R]` is a harmless generalization, not the source of drift.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.jt-m.justification: The blueprint says, “Every entry of the Jacobi–Trudi matrix H is a symmetric polynomial,” and the target quantifies over every entry via `(i j : Fin N)` and concludes `(jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam mu i j).IsSymmetric`. The dependency defines that entry exactly as `hsymmExt (↑(lam i) - ↑(mu j) - ↑↑i + ↑↑j)`, matching `h_{λᵢ - μⱼ - i + j}`; `hsymmExt` uses `MvPolynomial.hsymm` for nonnegative indices and `0` for negative indices, both within the intended extended complete homogeneous polynomials. `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric` means invariance under permutations of variables, matching the informal definition of symmetric polynomial. The binders `{R} [CommRing R]` and `{N : ℕ}` match the chapter setting of a commutative ring and N variables. Quantifying over arbitrary `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ`, rather than imposing partition conditions, only makes the theorem more general and does not weaken the claimed entrywise symmetry.

The target states exactly that `SymmetricFunctions.jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam mu = (... LGV.pathWeightMatrix ...).transpose`, matching “The Jacobi–Trudi matrix H equals the transpose of the LGV path weight matrix.” By the body of `LGV.pathWeightMatrix`, its `(i,j)` entry is `LGV.pathWeightSum ... (A i) (B j)`, and `LGV.pathWeightSum` is the sum of path weights over all paths from `A i` to `B j`, exactly matching `M_{i,j} = ∑_{p : A_i → B_j} w(p)`. The transpose therefore has `(i,j)` entry equal to the path-weight sum from `A_j` to `B_i`, as required for the Jacobi–Trudi entry. The binders `∀ {N} {R} [CommRing R] (lam mu : Fin N → ℕ)` merely make the matrix size, coefficient ring, and Jacobi–Trudi parameters explicit; allowing arbitrary `lam` and `mu` is at least as general as the blueprint and adds no restrictive hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.jt-s.justification: The binder `(∀ (i j : Fin N), i ≤ j → mu j ≤ mu i)` exactly encodes that `mu` is a weakly decreasing `N`-tuple of naturals, matching the informal hypothesis that an `N`-partition satisfies `μᵢ ≥ μⱼ` for `i ≤ j`. Expanding `jacobiTrudiSourceX` in the conclusion gives `↑(mu j) - ↑j ≤ ↑(mu i) - ↑i`, i.e. `μᵢ - i ≥ μⱼ - j`, as required. Although `Fin N` is zero-indexed while the blueprint writes indices `1,…,N`, translating a blueprint index `i` to `Fin` value `i-1` shifts every formal source coordinate by the same constant `+1`; this does not change the asserted weak-decreasing inequalities. Thus the formal theorem implies the blueprint statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.jt-t.justification: The formal binders encode exactly the partition condition and the desired monotonicity: `(∀ (i j : Fin N), i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i)` says that `lam` is weakly decreasing, matching an “N-partition” with `λ_i ≥ λ_j` for `i ≤ j`. Unfolding `jacobiTrudiTargetX`, the conclusion is `↑(lam j) - ↑↑j ≤ ↑(lam i) - ↑↑i`, which is the informal `λ_i - i ≥ λ_j - j`. Although `Fin N` is zero-based while the blueprint writes indices `1,…,N`, this only shifts every target x-coordinate by the same constant: the formal coordinate for index `i-1` is `λ_i-(i-1)=(λ_i-i)+1`, so the weak-decreasing inequality is unchanged. Quantifying over any weakly decreasing `lam : Fin N → ℕ`, rather than a bundled N-partition, is an equivalent/unbundled and harmlessly general formulation.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.latt.justification: The target quantifies without restrictions, `{N : ℕ} → {a c : ℤ} → ...`, while the blueprint describes genuine north/east paths “from `(a, 1)` to `(c, N)`.” The mismatch enters through `SymmetricFunctions.LatticePath.mk`, whose only endpoint-related condition is `eastStepHeights.length = (c - a).toNat`. Since `Int.toNat` sends negative differences to `0`, when `c < a` this type contains the empty list, although no north/east lattice path can move from x-coordinate `a` to the smaller x-coordinate `c`. Similarly, for `N = 0` and `c ≤ a`, the formal type can contain an empty encoding although no north/east path goes from height `1` to height `0`. Thus the formal equivalence is correctly an equivalence between its list encoding and `Sym (Fin N) (c-a).toNat`, and its forward and inverse maps match the stated extraction/sorting operations, but that encoding is not the blueprint’s endpoint-based path notion for all quantified parameters. On the usual valid range `a ≤ c` and `1 ≤ N`, the encoding agrees with the described paths. To repair the discrepancy, the setting and declaration would need those bounds, or `LatticePath` would need to encode genuine paths and endpoint feasibility; in the latter case the unrestricted right-hand side would also need adjustment, since `Sym (Fin N) 0` is inhabited in cases where the genuine path type is empty.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.lgv-.justification: The formal hypothesis “∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < vertices.length), LGV.integerLattice.arc …” says every consecutive pair is an integer-lattice step. By the body of `LGV.integerLattice`, each such step is either east, with unchanged y-coordinate, or north, increasing y by one. The definition `lgvPathEastStepYCoords` records exactly the starting y-coordinate of each east step, using the condition “v₁.1 = v₀.1 + 1 ∧ v₁.2 = v₀.2”. The conclusion “(vertices.head h_ne).2 ≤ y ∧ y ≤ (vertices.getLast h_ne).2” therefore exactly matches “y₀ ≤ y ≤ y₁” for a path whose start and end are its first and last vertices. The binder `h_ne : vertices ≠ []` merely makes those endpoints available and is inherent in describing a path from `(a, y₀)` to `(c, y₁)`, rather than an additional mathematical restriction.

The binder `h_ne : vertices ≠ []` and hypothesis `∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < vertices.length), LGV.integerLattice.arc ...` precisely encode a nonempty directed path vertex list. By the body of `LGV.integerLattice`, each consecutive step is either `(x,y) → (x+1,y)` or `(x,y) → (x,y+1)`, exactly the lattice arcs in `def.lgv.lattice`. The body of `SymmetricFunctions.lgvPathEastStepYCoords` adds one y-coordinate exactly in the first, east-step case. Thus its list length counts east-steps, and the conclusion equates that count with final x minus initial x. The use of `Int.toNat` is faithful because along such a directed lattice path the x-coordinate never decreases, so the displacement is nonnegative. The formal theorem is somewhat more general than the contextual conversion from `(a,1)` to `(c,N)`, since it applies to arbitrary endpoints, but this strengthening is faithful.

The blueprint says that “since paths can only go north or east, y-coordinates can only increase or stay the same along the path.” The formal hypothesis expresses exactly this path condition for every consecutive pair: `∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < vertices.length), LGV.integerLattice.arc ...`. By the body of `LGV.integerLattice`, each such arc is either east, `(x,y) → (x+1,y)`, or north, `(x,y) → (x,y+1)`. The definition `lgvPathEastStepYCoords` records `v₀.2` exactly when the consecutive step satisfies `v₁.1 = v₀.1 + 1 ∧ v₁.2 = v₀.2`, i.e. when it is east. The conclusion `List.IsChain (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) ...` states that adjacent extracted east-step heights are weakly increasing, matching the informal claim. The theorem does not impose the endpoints mentioned only in the contextual conversion definition, so it is at least as general as the blueprint statement.

The informal conversion is explicitly for an LGV path “from `(a, 1)` to `(c, N)`,” and the target quantifies paths with exactly those endpoint conditions: `hstart₁ : p₁.start = (a, 1)`, `hfinish₁ : p₁.finish = (c, ↑N)` and likewise for `p₂`. Thus these are domain-encoding hypotheses, not added mathematical restrictions. Equality of `lgvPathToLatticePath ...` equates the converted east-step-height lists; by the dependency body, these are obtained from `lgvPathEastStepYCoords p.vertices` via `lgvYCoordsToFinN`, exactly implementing the informal definition of extracting east-step y-coordinates and subtracting 1. The conclusion `p₁ = p₂` implies that the paths have the same vertex sequence, as required by “two LGV paths with the same east-step y-coordinates have the same vertex sequence,” and is an acceptable stronger formulation of that conclusion.

The target exactly states the claimed equality: `LGV.pathWeight SymmetricFunctions.jacobiTrudiArcWeight p = (SymmetricFunctions.lgvPathToLatticePath a c p hstart hfinish).weight`. Its binders restrict `p` precisely as required by the informal conversion definition, namely `hstart : p.start = (a, 1)` and `hfinish : p.finish = (c, ↑N)`, matching “an LGV path ... from `(a, 1)` to `(c, N)`.” The dependency bodies also match the stated meanings: `jacobiTrudiArcWeight` assigns `X ⟨(u.2 - 1).toNat, ...⟩` to east-steps at heights `1 ≤ u.2 ≤ N` and `1` otherwise, while `LatticePath.weight` is the product of `MvPolynomial.X j` over the converted east-step heights. The arbitrary `[CommRing R]` supplies the coefficient setting needed by these polynomial and path-weight definitions and does not introduce a mathematically conflicting restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.m-co.justification: The target quantifies over exactly the relevant objects, `∀ ... {N : ℕ} (mu nu : ...NPartition N), mu ≠ nu → ... = 0`, matching “for any two distinct N-partitions μ ≠ ν.” Its coefficient expression `MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm mu.parts) (monomialSymm nu)` is the coefficient of the exponent tuple `mu.parts`, hence of `x^μ`, in `m_ν`. The dependency `monomialSymm nu := ∑ a ∈ sortPreimage nu, monomialExp a` implements the informal definition `m_ν = ∑_{sort(a)=ν} x^a`; the finite bound in `sortPreimage` does not narrow this set, since every entry of a tuple sorting to ν is at most the sum `NPartition.size ν`. The formal binder `[CommSemiring R]` is weaker than the blueprint’s fixed commutative-ring setting, so the theorem is strictly more general and in particular implies the stated result for the fixed commutative ring K.

The target states for every `mu : NPartition N` that `MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm mu.parts) (monomialSymm mu) = 1`, exactly matching “the coefficient of x^{μ} ... in m_μ is 1.” Here `mu.parts : Fin N → ℕ` represents the exponent tuple, and `monomialSymm mu` is defined as the sum of `monomialExp a` over tuples sorting to `mu`, matching the informal definition of `m_μ`. Although `sortPreimage` includes the bound `a i < mu.size + 1`, this does not mathematically narrow the tuples satisfying `sortTuple a = mu`: each entry then is an entry of `mu` and hence at most their sum `mu.size`. The formal binder `[inst : CommSemiring R]` is weaker than the blueprint context’s fixed commutative ring `K`, so the theorem is strictly more general rather than weaker. Likewise, explicitly quantifying `R` and `N` generalizes the chapter’s fixed choices.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.m-ho.justification: The target states `∀ {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {N : ℕ} (mu : ...NPartition N), (monomialSymm mu).IsHomogeneous (NPartition.size mu)`, exactly matching “The monomial symmetric polynomial m_μ is homogeneous of degree |μ|.” The dependencies identify `monomialSymm mu` with the sum of monomials whose exponent tuples sort to `mu`, `NPartition.size mu` with the sum of μ’s entries, and `MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous` with all occurring monomials having that degree. The blueprint fixes a commutative ring `K` and an `N`, whereas Lean quantifies over every `CommSemiring R` and every `N`; this is strictly more general, not a weakening, since every commutative ring supplies the required commutative-semiring structure.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.m-sy.justification: The blueprint says, “For any N-partition μ, the polynomial m_μ is symmetric.” The target states exactly `∀ {R} [CommSemiring R] {N} (mu : ...NPartition N), (monomialSymm mu).IsSymmetric`. Here `NPartition N` is the specified weakly decreasing N-tuple, `monomialSymm` is the sum of `monomialExp a` over tuples satisfying `sortTuple a = mu`, and `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric` means invariance under permutations of variables. The finite bound in `sortPreimage` does not narrow the intended sum: if `sortTuple a = μ`, every entry of `a` is an entry of μ and hence is at most `NPartition.size μ`, exactly the values included by `Finset.range (size μ + 1)`. The informal setting fixes a commutative ring, whereas the formal binder only requires `[CommSemiring R]`; this is a strictly more general coefficient class, not an added restriction, so the formal theorem still implies the blueprint statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.m-ze.justification: The target exactly formalizes “When $N>0$, $m_{(0,0,\ldots,0)}=1$”: its binder `(hN : 0 < N)` is precisely the stated positivity condition, and `singletonPartition 0 hN` has parts `(0,0,…,0)`. By the body of `monomialSymm`, the left side is the sum of `monomialExp a` over `sortPreimage`; these definitions match the informal definitions of $m_\lambda$, the sort preimage, and $x^a$. The formal coefficient assumption `[CommSemiring R]` is weaker than the blueprint’s fixed commutative ring $K$, so the theorem is strictly more general rather than weakened by an added hypothesis. The universal binders over `R` and `N` appropriately generalize the chapter’s fixed parameters.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.mem-.justification: The formal binders match the blueprint hypotheses exactly: `(hcontained : mu ≤ lam)` expresses “μ ⊆ λ” because `NPartition.partLE` is componentwise comparison; `{ outer := lam, inner := mu, contained := hcontained }.isHorizontalNStrip n` expresses “λ/μ is a horizontal n-strip”; and `(∀ (i : Fin N), lam.parts i ≤ horizontalStripUpperBound mu n i)` is precisely the stated upper-bound constraint. The conclusion `lam ∈ horizontalNStripPartitions mu n` matches membership in the finite set from the informal definition. The bundled skew partition’s containment proof is not an added restriction: it is the formal encoding of the explicitly assumed `μ ⊆ λ`. Its horizontal-strip and size definitions also agree with the blueprint under that containment.

The target directly formalizes the implication: its binder `(hcontained : mu ≤ lam)` matches “If μ ⊆ λ,” since `NPartition.instLE` uses `partLE`, defined as `∀ i, mu.parts i ≤ lam.parts i`. Its premise `{ outer := lam, inner := mu, contained := hcontained }.isVerticalNStrip n` matches “λ/μ is a vertical n-strip”: `isVerticalNStrip` is `isVerticalStrip ∧ size = n`, where `isVerticalStrip` requires `lam.parts i ≤ mu.parts i + 1` and the bundled skew partition already carries containment. Finally, the conclusion `lam ∈ verticalNStripPartitions mu n` is exactly membership in the finite set described by the informal definition. The finset body enumerates componentwise values between `mu_i` and `mu_i + 1`, filters for a weakly decreasing partition and size difference `n`, so its meaning agrees with vertical n-strip partitions. There are no additional mathematically substantive hypotheses.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.mini.justification: The target states `∀ {N : ℕ} (lam : Fin N → ℕ), contentTableau (minimalisticTableau lam) = lam`, while the blueprint states this for `λ` an `N`-partition. The formal quantifier allows every tuple `Fin N → ℕ`, without requiring weak decrease, so it is strictly more general rather than weaker and in particular implies the blueprint case. The definitions agree with the intended objects: `minimalisticTableau lam c => (↑c).1` fills each cell with its row index, and `contentTableau T i => Nat.card { c // T c = i }` counts cells carrying `i`. For shape `lam/zeroTuple`, those cells are exactly the cells in row `i`, whose columns satisfy `0 < j ∧ j ≤ lam i`, hence there are `lam i` of them. Thus the asserted function equality is precisely `cont(T₀) = λ` on all `N`-partitions.

The blueprint says: “The minimalistic tableau T₀ of shape λ (where T₀(i,j) = i for all cells) is semistandard.” Formally, `minimalisticTableau lam` has body `fun c => (↑c).1`, so each entry is exactly its row index. `IsSemistandard` requires weak increase for cells in the same row with increasing columns and strict increase for cells in the same column with increasing rows, matching the stated row and column conditions. The target quantifies over every `lam : Fin N → ℕ`, whereas the blueprint assumes λ is an N-partition. This is a strictly more general statement, not an added restriction: the result remains true without weak decrease of `lam`. The use of `Fin N` gives a zero-based encoding of both row indices and entries, but preserves their equality and order, so it does not change the mathematical assertion.

The elaborated theorem quantifies over exactly the required data: `∀ {N : ℕ} (lam : Fin N → ℕ), IsNPartition lam → ∀ (T : Tableau lam zeroTuple), IsYamanouchi zeroTuple T → T = minimalisticTableau lam`. This matches “Let λ be an N-partition. If T is a 0-Yamanouchi semistandard tableau of shape λ/0, then T is the minimalistic tableau T₀.” The dependencies preserve the intended meanings: `IsNPartition` is weak decrease; `Tableau lam zeroTuple` consists of fillings of the 1-indexed diagram `0 < j ≤ lam i`; `IsYamanouchi` includes `IsSemistandard T` and requires the restricted-column content to be an N-partition for every `j > 0`; and `minimalisticTableau lam c = (↑c).1` assigns each cell its row label. The use of `Fin N` gives the standard zero-based encoding of the blueprint’s labels `[N]`, consistently for both rows and entries, and introduces no substantive restriction.

The target quantifies over exactly the required data, `∀ {N : ℕ} (lam : Fin N → ℕ), IsNPartition lam → ...`, matching “Let λ be an N-partition.” Its conclusion is `IsYamanouchi zeroTuple (minimalisticTableau lam)`. By the dependency bodies, `minimalisticTableau lam` has type `Tableau lam zeroTuple` and sends each cell to its row index (`fun ... c => (↑c).1`), while `IsYamanouchi` unfolds to `IsSemistandard T ∧ ∀ j > 0, IsNPartition (nu + contentColGeq T j)`. Thus it asserts both semistandardness and the required partition condition for every positive column cutoff, exactly the informal claim that the row-index filling of shape `λ/0` is `0`-Yamanouchi. The use of `Fin N` is the standard zero-based encoding of the informal indices `[N]` and preserves their order; allowing `N = 0` is, at most, a harmless generalization.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.mono.justification: The blueprint states “the degree of the product of two monomials is the sum of their degrees.” The formal declaration quantifies over arbitrary `{N : ℕ}` and `m₁ m₂ : Monomial N` and concludes `(m₁ + m₂).degree = m₁.degree + m₂.degree`. Here `Monomial N` is `Fin N →₀ ℕ`, so its inherited addition is pointwise addition of exponent vectors, exactly representing multiplication of monomials. Moreover, `Monomial.degree` is `Finsupp.sum m (fun x a => a)`, matching the informal definition as the sum of exponents. There are no additional hypotheses or restricted quantifiers.

The target states `∀ {N : ℕ} (m : Monomial N), m.IsSquarefree → m.degree ≤ N`, exactly matching “A squarefree monomial has degree at most N.” The dependency bodies preserve the blueprint meanings: `Monomial N = Fin N →₀ ℕ` represents the N exponents; `IsSquarefree m := ∀ (i : Fin N), m i ≤ 1` is equivalent for natural exponents to each exponent lying in `{0,1}`; and `degree m := Finsupp.sum m fun x a => a` sums those exponents. Quantifying over `N` is more general than the chapter convention fixing an arbitrary `N`, and introduces no restrictive hypothesis. The fixed commutative ring `K` is irrelevant because this statement concerns exponent vectors only.

The blueprint says that a primal monomial is exactly “m = 1 or m = x_i^k for some i ∈ [N] and some k > 0.” Under `Monomial N := Fin N →₀ ℕ`, the multiplicative monomial `1` is represented by the zero exponent vector, so the target’s `m = 0` is the correct encoding. The term `(fun₀ | i => k)` is `Finsupp.single i k`, the exponent vector having exponent `k` at `i : Fin N` and zero elsewhere, hence represents `x_i^k`; the conjunct `0 < k` matches `k > 0`. Finally, `m.IsPrimal` unfolds to `m.support.card ≤ 1`, which exactly expresses the informal definition that at most one exponent is positive. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

The declarations collectively assert every part of the blueprint: for every `s : Finset (Fin N)`, `ofFinset s` is defined by `∑ x ∈ s, fun₀ | x => 1`, i.e. the exponent vector that is `1` exactly on `s`; `toPoly_ofFinset` states `(ofFinset s).toPoly = ∏ i ∈ s, MvPolynomial.X i`, matching `𝔪_S = ∏_{i ∈ S} x_i`; `isSquarefree_ofFinset` states `(ofFinset s).IsSquarefree`, where `IsSquarefree` means `∀ i, m i ≤ 1`, equivalent for natural exponents to belonging to `{0,1}`; `degree_ofFinset` states `(ofFinset s).degree = s.card`, matching degree `|S|`; and `support_ofFinset` states `(ofFinset s).support = s`. Representing `[N] = {1,…,N}` by the canonically N-element type `Fin N` is an index-shift encoding, not a mathematical restriction. The universal binders over `N` and, for the polynomial identity, over every `[CommRing K]` are at least as general as the blueprint context fixing a commutative ring `K` and a natural number `N`.

The body `fun ... m => (MvPolynomial.monomial m) 1` exactly constructs the multivariate monomial with exponent vector `m` and coefficient `1`; the base-library specification says that `MvPolynomial.monomial s a` has “coefficient `a` and exponents given by `s`.” With `Monomial N := Fin N →₀ ℕ` and `P K N := MvPolynomial (Fin N) K`, this is precisely the polynomial `x₁^{a₁} ⋯ x_N^{a_N}` described informally. The stated zero-vector, standard-basis-vector, and addition/product cases are consequences of this construction. The binders `{K : Type u_1} → [CommRing K] → {N : ℕ}` do not introduce drift: `P` itself is defined over a `CommRing K`, and quantifying over arbitrary such `K` is at least as general as the coefficient-unspecified blueprint statement.

The two declarations exactly formalize the two blueprint clauses. `monomialExp_coeff_self` states for every exponent tuple `a : Fin N → ℕ` that `coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm a) (monomialExp a) = 1`, matching “The coefficient of $x^a$ in $x^a$ is $1$.” Likewise, `monomialExp_coeff_ne` assumes `a ≠ b` and concludes `coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm b) (monomialExp a) = 0`, matching “The coefficient of $x^b$ in $x^a$ is $0$ when $a \neq b$.” The dependency defines `monomialExp a` as `∏ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ a i`, exactly the informal monomial $x^a=\prod_i x_i^{a_i}$. The equivalence merely converts the finite tuple `b : Fin N → ℕ` into the finitely supported exponent representation expected by `MvPolynomial.coeff`. The universally quantified coefficient type `[CommSemiring R]` supplies the polynomial setting and makes the result more general; it does not narrow the informal assertion.

The blueprint says, “The total degree of $x^a$ equals $\sum_i a_i$,” with $x^a=x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_N^{a_N}$. The dependency defines `monomialExp a` exactly as `∏ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ a i`, and the target concludes `(monomialExp a).totalDegree = ∑ i, a i`, with `i : Fin N`, matching all $N$ entries. The binders `[CommSemiring R] [Nontrivial R]` encode the auxiliary realization of the syntactic monomial as an `MvPolynomial`; `Nontrivial R` prevents all coefficients, including `1`, from collapsing to zero, which would make library `totalDegree` fail to represent the syntactic degree. It does not restrict the exponent tuple `a : Fin N → ℕ` from the blueprint.

The target quantifies over exactly an exponent tuple, `∀ ... {N : ℕ} (a : Fin N → ℕ)`, and asserts `monomialExp a = MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm a) 1`. By the dependency body, `monomialExp a` is `∏ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ a i`, matching the blueprint’s `x^a = ∏ᵢ x_i^{a_i}`. Since `Fin N` is finite, `Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm a` is precisely the finitely supported exponent representation of the tuple `a`, and `MvPolynomial.monomial ... 1` is the Mathlib monomial with those exponents and coefficient `1`. The binder `[CommSemiring R]` supplies the coefficient setting required by `MvPolynomial`; allowing every commutative semiring is a general coefficient choice and does not narrow the blueprint statement.

The two declarations exactly formalize the two asserted identities. `monomialExp_add` quantifies over exponent tuples `(a b : Fin N → ℕ)` and concludes `monomialExp (a + b) = monomialExp a * monomialExp b`, matching “$x^{a+b} = x^a \cdot x^b$.” `monomialExp_zero` concludes `monomialExp 0 = 1`, matching “$x^0 = 1$.” The dependency defines `monomialExp a` as `∏ i, MvPolynomial.X i ^ a i`, which is precisely the monomial $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_N^{a_N}$ from `def.sf.monomial`. Although the signatures assume only `[CommSemiring R]` rather than the blueprint’s commutative-ring setting, this is a weaker hypothesis and therefore a valid strict generalization, not drift.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.nipa.justification: The target states an actual type equivalence, `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat lam mu hlam hmu hcontained ≃ SymmetricFunctions.SkewSSYT { outer := … lam …, inner := … mu …, contained := … }`, exactly matching the blueprint’s `Nipat(λ, μ) ≃ SkewSSYT(λ/μ)`. Its `toFun := SymmetricFunctions.nipatToSSYT` and `invFun := SymmetricFunctions.ssytToNipat`, together with the two inverse laws, also match the stated “forward and inverse maps.” The binders `hlam`, `hmu`, and `hcontained` merely supply the weakly decreasing and containment data required to construct the partitions λ, μ and the skew shape λ/μ; they encode the objects appearing in the blueprint rather than add unrelated hypotheses.

The target states for every `np : SymmetricFunctions.Nipat lam mu hlam hmu hcontained` that `np.weight = (SymmetricFunctions.nipatToSSYT np).toMonomial`, exactly matching “for every nipat p, w(p) = x_{T(p)}.” The referenced bodies preserve the intended meanings: `Nipat.weight` is `∏ i, (np.paths i).weight`; `LatticePath.weight` multiplies `MvPolynomial.X j` over all east-step heights; `nipatToSSYT` uses those same heights as tableau entries; and `SkewSSYT.toMonomial` multiplies `MvPolynomial.X (T.entries i j)` over all boxes. Thus both sides multiply the same variable once per east step/tableau box. The binders `hlam`, `hmu`, and `hcontained` encode that λ and μ are N-partitions with μ ⊆ λ, as required by the informal definitions. The universally quantified `[CommRing R]` is a coefficient-ring setting needed by the project’s weight and monomial definitions, not an additional restriction on the nipats covered by the blueprint statement.

The formal theorem adds the mathematically substantive binder `hcontained : ∀ (i : Fin N), mu i ≤ lam i`, whereas the blueprint defines the skew Schur polynomial for “two N-partitions” without requiring containment and explicitly says that when `μ ⊈ λ`, there are no tableaux. Thus the informal equality also covers the non-contained case, where both sides should be empty sums. The restriction enters not only in the target but in the dependencies: `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat ... hcontained`, `SymmetricFunctions.SkewPartition.mk ... inner ≤ outer`, and hence `SymmetricFunctions.skewSchur : SkewPartition N → ...` all require containment. To be faithful, these notions should be extended to arbitrary pairs of N-partitions, with the nipat/tableau collections empty when containment fails, and the target’s `hcontained` binder removed. The additional `[CommRing R]` is an algebraic setting/generalization and is not the source of drift.

The blueprint quantifies over two N-partitions without requiring containment: “Let λ and μ be two N-partitions,” and explicitly fixes the noncontained case by saying, “If we don’t have μ ⊆ λ, then we agree that there are no Young tableaux of shape λ/μ.” The target instead has the additional binder `(hcontained : ∀ (i : Fin N), mu i ≤ lam i)`, so it only proves the equality when μ ⊆ λ. This restriction is built into both relevant project index types: `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat ... (hcontained : ∀ i, mu i ≤ lam i) → Type`, while `SymmetricFunctions.SkewSSYT` takes a `SkewPartition`, whose constructor likewise requires `inner ≤ outer`. Consequently, the project's supplied definitions do not denote either side of the blueprint equation for noncontained λ, μ, despite the blueprint assigning both the intended empty-set interpretation. To make the statement faithful, the dependencies must be extended with versions of `Nipat` and `SkewSSYT` defined for arbitrary pairs of N-partitions and empty when containment fails (or equivalent wrapper definitions implementing that convention); then `nipatWeightSum_eq_ssytSum` should omit `hcontained` and quantify over all two N-partitions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.non-.justification: The target has exactly the required partition hypotheses: `IsNPartition lam → IsNPartition mu → IsNPartition nu → ...`, matching “For N-partitions λ, μ, ν”. Its implicit summation index is supplied by `nonYamanouchiTableau_fintype`, whose underlying subtype is `{ T // IsSemistandard T ∧ ¬ IsYamanouchi nu T }`, exactly the tableaux in `SSYT(λ/μ)` that are not ν-Yamanouchi. The summand `alternant (nu + contentTableau ↑T + rho N)` matches `a_{ν + cont(T) + ρ}`, and the conclusion is equality to zero in `MvPolynomial (Fin N) R`. The binder `[CommRing R]` matches the chapter’s fixed commutative coefficient ring; universally quantifying it is more general, not an added restriction. Although the formal `Tableau lam mu` does not enforce the informal convention that there are no tableaux when `μ ⊈ λ`, the theorem requires no `μ ⊆ λ` hypothesis and proves cancellation even for those additional formal tableaux. On the intended valid skew shapes the definitions coincide, while outside them the formal assertion is stronger than the blueprint’s empty-sum case, so this does not weaken the formalization.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.npar.justification: The formalization captures both clauses. The blueprint says, “The componentwise sum of two $N$-partitions is an $N$-partition,” and `NPartition.add` has signature `{N : ℕ} → NPartition N → NPartition N → NPartition N` with entries `parts := fun i => μ.parts i + ν.parts i`; its result type and `antitone` field establish that this componentwise sum is again an `NPartition N`. The second clause, “$|\mu + \nu| = |\mu| + |\nu|$,” is exactly the target `∀ {N : ℕ} (μ ν : NPartition N), (μ + ν).size = μ.size + ν.size`. Moreover, `NPartition.size` is `∑ i, μ.parts i`, matching the informal definition of size. There are no additional hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

The target states `∀ {N : ℕ} {μ ν : NPartition N}, μ ≤ ν ↔ μ.youngDiagram ⊆ ν.youngDiagram`, exactly matching “μ ≤ ν if and only if Y(μ) ⊆ Y(ν).” The meanings also align: `NPartition.instLE` defines `μ ≤ ν` as `∀ (i : Fin N), μ.parts i ≤ ν.parts i`, matching componentwise comparison for all indices, while `NPartition.youngDiagram` unions the cells `(i,j)` for `i : Fin N` and `j ∈ Finset.range (μ.parts i)`, i.e. `j < μ_i`. The use of zero-based `Fin N` rather than `[N]` is explicitly sanctioned by the informal convention and does not alter the equivalence. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

The target quantifies over the same fixed length and partitions, `∀ {N : ℕ} {μ ν : NPartition N}`, and assumes exactly `μ ≤ ν`. By `NPartition.instLE`, this means `∀ (i : Fin N), μ.parts i ≤ ν.parts i`, matching “μ ≤ ν (componentwise)” and the definition “μᵢ ≤ νᵢ for all i ∈ [N].” Its conclusion `μ.size ≤ ν.size` matches `|μ| ≤ |ν|`, since `NPartition.size` is `∑ i, μ.parts i`, exactly the sum of all N entries. `NPartition` itself consists of antitone `Fin N → ℕ` functions, matching weakly decreasing N-tuples of nonnegative integers. No additional hypothesis or restricted quantifier is introduced.

The formal definition `fun {N} μ => {i | μ.parts i ≠ 0}.card` exactly counts the nonzero entries of the `Fin N → ℕ` tuple, matching “the length … is the number of nonzero entries.” The theorem `∀ {N : ℕ} (μ : NPartition N), μ.length ≤ N` matches `ℓ(λ) ≤ N`, and `∀ {N : ℕ} {μ : NPartition N}, μ.length = 0 ↔ μ = 0` matches `ℓ(λ) = 0 ↔ λ = (0,…,0)`, since `NPartition.zero` has every part equal to zero. The dependency `NPartition.mk … (parts : Fin N → ℕ) → Antitone parts` faithfully represents a weakly decreasing N-tuple of natural numbers. There are no additional mathematically contentful hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

Both declarations exactly match the two blueprint claims under the stated existence conditions. For rows, the formal binders `∀ (N n : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)` agree with the informal definition’s “Requires `N > 0`,” and `rowPartition` has parts `if ↑i = 0 then n else 0`; its `size := ∑ i, parts i` is therefore `n`, matching “The row partition `(n, 0, …, 0)` has size `n`.” For columns, the formal binders `∀ (N n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ N)` exactly match “with `n` ones, `n ≤ N`,” while `colPartition` has parts `if ↑i < n then 1 else 0`; summing over `Fin N` gives `n`, matching the asserted size. The conditions `0 < N` and `n ≤ N` are not added drift: they are explicitly required by the corresponding informal definitions and are needed for these `N`-partitions to have the described forms.

The formal declarations match both bullets and the defining notation. For the first bullet, the blueprint says “Each entry is bounded by the size: λᵢ ≤ |λ| for all i,” and `NPartition.parts_le_size` quantifies `∀ {N : ℕ} (μ : NPartition N) (i : Fin N), μ.parts i ≤ μ.size`; `Fin N` ranges over exactly the N entries, while `NPartition.size` is defined as `∑ i, μ.parts i`. For the second bullet, the blueprint says “|λ| = 0 if and only if λ = (0, …, 0),” and `NPartition.size_eq_zero_iff` states `μ.size = 0 ↔ μ = 0`, with `NPartition.zero` defined by the constantly-zero parts function. `NPartition.eq_zero_of_size_eq_zero` additionally states the forward implication and is consistent with the biconditional. Both `NPartition` representations require natural-valued weakly decreasing parts, exactly the informal definition, and `SymmetricFunctions.NPartition.size` likewise defines size as the sum of all parts. Allowing arbitrary `N : ℕ`, including zero, is at most a harmless generalization because the informal statement imposes no positivity condition on N.

The target states `∀ {N : ℕ} (lam mu : NPartition N), (lam.skewYoungDiagram mu).card = ∑ i, (lam.parts i - mu.parts i)`, matching `|Y(λ/μ)| = ∑_{i=1}^N (λ_i - μ_i)`. The formal `skewYoungDiagram` is exactly `lam.youngDiagram \ mu.youngDiagram`; its 0-indexed columns differ from the informal 1-indexed convention only by a cardinality-preserving shift. Although the informal definition introduces `Y(λ/μ)` under `μ ⊆ λ`, the target has no such hypothesis and is therefore strictly more general: natural subtraction correctly counts each row of the set difference even without containment. Under the informal condition `μ ≤ λ` (componentwise), the displayed sum also equals `|λ| - |μ|` by the given definition of partition size, so the target implies the statement’s second sentence as well.

The target states `∀ {N : ℕ} (μ : NPartition N), μ.youngDiagram.card = μ.size`, exactly matching “The cardinality of the Young diagram equals the size: `|Y(λ)| = |λ|`.” The dependencies implement the blueprint definitions: `NPartition.size` is `∑ i, μ.parts i`, while `NPartition.youngDiagram` unions, for every `i : Fin N`, the cells `(i,j)` with `j ∈ Finset.range (μ.parts i)`. Thus each row has `μ.parts i` cells and the total cardinality is the sum of the entries. The formal use of zero-based `Fin N` and `range` instead of the blueprint’s one-based `[N]` and `[λᵢ]` is only a bijective indexing convention and does not change the asserted cardinality. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers.

The target quantifies over every N-partition and every row, `∀ {N : ℕ} (μ : NPartition N) (i : Fin N)`, and concludes `{c ∈ μ.youngDiagram | c.1 = i}.card = μ.parts i`, exactly asserting that the number of diagram cells whose row coordinate is `i` equals the corresponding part. The dependency `NPartition.youngDiagram` contains, for each `i`, precisely the cells `(i,j)` with `j ∈ Finset.range (μ.parts i)`, so that row has `μ.parts i` cells. Using `Fin N` and zero-based `Finset.range` instead of the informal one-based sets `[N]` and `[λ_i]` is a harmless indexing representation and preserves cardinality. stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.omeg.justification: The formal conclusion exactly expresses entrywise commutation with determinant: ` (omegaInvolution hn) M.det = (M.map ⇑(omegaInvolution hn)).det`, matching “`ω(det(M)) = det(ω(M))`, where `ω(M)` applies `ω` entry-wise.” The matrix binder `M : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ↥(MvPolynomial.symmetricSubalgebra σ R)` ranges over arbitrary square matrices of arbitrary natural size `m` over the symmetric subalgebra.
